title: Midyear Career Checklist & Evidence Bank - Jordan Kim
content:
Purpose and how to use this doc:
- Quick, utilitarian scratchpad to assemble the narrative + raw evidence I want to bring to midyear 1:1 / self-review / calibration.
- Not polished — two goals: (1) make it trivial to extract 3–5 strong bullets for my self-review and promotion packet, (2) leave a short list of asks and next-step experiments to discuss with manager.

Timebox: 45 minutes before 1:1 to update with freshest metrics / links / feedback snippets.

Current role context (1 sentence):
Senior People Operations Partner supporting eng infra and platform orgs (~40 ICs + 6 managers). Focus areas: onboarding & ramp, manager enablement, hiring process ops.

Primary objectives for H1 2026 (personal translation of OKRs):
- O1: Reduce new-hire time-to-first-PR for infra by 20% (measure: days from first commit/TS to first merged PR).
- O2: Establish a lightweight manager coaching program and run pilot with 6 managers; target 80% satisfaction in post-pilot survey.
- O3: Remove friction from interview scheduling for 3 highest-traffic roles (automation + vendor integration) and reduce average scheduling time by 50%.

Progress highlights (evidence snippets):
- Onboarding ramp: initiated "ramp checklist v2" with eng platform leads; rolled out to two teams on 2026-01-18. Early metric: average days to first PR for pilot cohort = 18 days (baseline last quarter = 26 days) -> 31% improvement (raw numbers in JIRA-OPS-1289).
- Manager enablement: designed 6-session pilot (60–90m modules), ran first cohort Jan–Feb with 6 managers across infra and observability. Post-pilot survey: 83% reported at least one behavior they will implement; sample verbatim: "The 1:1 framework changed how I prep - lost fewer action items." (see Confluence-4521/surveys).
- Scheduling automation: prototype integration with Calendly + recruiting scheduler scripts reduced manual follow-up. Sample reduction in scheduling time: from 24h avg to 9h avg for role: infra-sr-sw (pilot metrics attached).
- Cross-functional impact: partnered with Recruiting on offer timeline analysis; flagged 2 process steps adding average 2 days to offers. Raised a transferable recommendation that reduced offer cycle by 1.2 days per case for pilot teams.

Concrete metrics (pull these into review):
- New-hire PR ramp: pilot cohort mean = 18 days; median = 16 days; N = 12.
- Manager pilot satisfaction: 83% positive (n=6).
- Scheduling time improvement for targeted roles: avg 24h -> 9h (63% reduction) during pilot (n=23 processes).
- One-off escalations avoided: 4 escalations prevented due to improved onboarding doc & triage flow.

Qualitative examples / quotes to cite (short raw quotes):
- "Onboarding flow got me productive faster — clear first tasks were gold." — new hire, infra team, 2026-02-08.
- "Jordan's coaching template made 1:1s more actionable." — manager pilot participant.
- Email excerpt from Eng Manager (Priya): "Your checklist caught a critical gap in our repo access; prevented a week delay."

Risk, gaps, and mitigation I want to discuss:
- Risk: pilot cohorts small; metric drift possible once scaled. Mitigation: schedule A/B rollout with control teams and instrument more telemetry (repo events, slack join -> first PR).
- Gap: I still need an automated dashboard; currently manual pulls are time-consuming. Ask: 2-day dev resource from Analytics to automate weekly dashboard (estimate 10 hours dev).
- People risk: managers' time to participate. Mitigation ask: exec sponsor note to managers + 1-hour comp for attendance (proposal below).

Promotion / growth storyline (draft talking points):
- Theme: "Operationalizing onboarding and manager effectiveness for long-term engine scaling."
- Problem: onboarding and manager enablement were manual, causing variability in ramp and manager quality.
- Approach: built repeatable artifacts (ramp checklist, coaching modules, scheduling automation), ran pilots, measured improvements, iterated with stakeholders.
- Outcomes: demonstrated measurable improvement in ramp times and manager satisfaction; created repeatable playbook ready to scale.
- Next level impact: I want to own scaled rollout for all infra/platform teams + lead ops integration with analytics for continuous measurement.

Specific asks for manager (short list):
- Sponsor the dashboard automation request (assign 8–10 hours from analytics or product ops).
- Approve pilot budget for manager sessions (covers external facilitator + small stipends) — ~$3k.
- Introduce me to head of platform-eng for expanded rollout and to align on performance metrics.
- Consider calibration for promotion discussion: I believe my impact and scope have expanded beyond current IC level; would like feedback on readiness for Staff People Ops role.

Draft phrases for self-review and promotion packet (pick 3–5):
- "Spearheaded a reproducible onboarding program that reduced mean time-to-first-PR for pilot cohorts by 31%, improving new hire productivity and reducing manager overhead."
- "Designed and launched a manager enablement pilot that 83% of participants rated as immediately actionable, resulting in cleaner 1:1 outcomes and fewer follow-up escalations."
- "Built cross-functional automation and playbooks that shortened interview scheduling times by 63% for high-volume roles, reducing candidate friction and recruiter time."

Calibration evidence to attach (quick checklist):
- links to: Confluence-4521 (manager pilot notes + survey), JIRA-OPS-1289 (onboarding ramp tickets), scheduling-pilot-report.xlsx, candidate-feedback-summaries.pdf, selected emails (Priya-endorsement.msg).

Open questions I want manager's perspective on:
- Is the magnitude of metric improvement (18 days -> 26 days baseline) sufficient to be considered above-expectation for promotion?
- Which of these two scaling approaches would you prefer: (A) central ops-run rollout with templates and minimal embedding vs (B) org-embedded rollout where each team owns a tailored checklist?
- Any additional stakeholders I should loop in before wider rollout?

Immediate next actions (this doc as a checklist):
- [ ] Pull final numbers from analytics and paste here (today, 30m).
- [ ] Add one strong anecdote from a hiring manager (ask Priya for short quote).
- [ ] Draft 1-page ask for analytics dev time + budget note for manager approval (2 hours).
- [ ] Prepare 3-slide summary for 1:1 (impact, ask, next steps) (1 hour).

Notes to self (scratch):
- Keep the promotion phrasing crisp and metric-forward. Avoid long process descriptions in the packet.
- If manager asks for more scale evidence, propose a 90-day A/B rollout with control cohort.

Version history/edits:
- 2026-02-20 initial draft (baseline metrics pulled).
- 2026-02-28 added manager pilot survey results.
- 2026-03-10 updated ramp numbers from analytics and added scheduling pilot details.

End of doc.
